assessment.nobel_worthiness: Biomolecular condensates reframed intracellular organisation as liquid-liquid phase separation, a general phase-behaviour principle applied to a messy living system. The concept is new, simple, and has reorganised cell biology, disease (including amyloid-linked aggregation) and biophysical chemistry. This is the kind of reduction of biological complexity to physical-chemical principles I value most.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne made the foundational P-granule demonstration of liquid-like droplets in cells; Rosen's multivalent-interaction work supplied the quantitative physical framework. Pappu and Mittag are strong on sequence grammar and sticker-spacer ideas, so a three-person cut leaves out meaningful contributors and credit remains contestable.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many independent labs over about 15 years and highly cited, so timing is not premature. The interpretation is still debated, since liquid-like behaviour in vivo does not always prove functional phase separation.
uncertainties: Debate on whether condensates are truly equilibrium phase separation in cells and on their functional relevance versus artefacts of overexpression
Fair allocation among Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, Pappu and Mittag, with possible overlap with a medicine or physics framing
I rely on my own recollection of the field and have not independently verified details

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are lipid self-assembly and pH-dependent phase behaviour turned into a delivery technology, and they enabled the mRNA vaccines and siRNA therapeutics. The impact on health and the clear link to lipid physical chemistry (ionisable headgroup pKa, fusogenic non-bilayer phases, microfluidic assembly) make it highly worthy.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and colleagues (Madden, Hope, MacLachlan) developed the ionizable lipid and rapid-mixing LNP formulation; Anderson and Langer contributed lipidoid libraries and delivery screening. Credit is spread over several people and companies, and the mRNA vaccine prize to Karikó and Weissman already sits adjacent, so I propose the two most distinct lines but acknowledge that the three-person limit forces hard choices.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated at very large scale, with strong independent confirmation, so recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Whether the Academy sees this as chemistry or medicine/pharmaceutics
Allocation among Cullis, Madden, Hope, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer is unresolved
Patent and commercial disputes may colour attribution

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation by PROTACs and molecular glues introduced a new chemical modality that reprograms the ubiquitin-proteasome system by induced proximity, opening 'undruggable' targets. The concept is original and has become a major drug discovery paradigm, with chemistry-driven design of ternary complexes and cooperativity.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and first demonstrated PROTACs; Ciulli provided VHL ligands and structural/thermodynamic understanding of ternary complexes. The molecular glue lineage (Handa, Ito, Kim, Gray) is a separate, compound strand that may need separate recognition, so credit is not cleanly resolved.
assessment.maturity: Many degraders are now in late-stage clinical trials but approval-level proof is still emerging, which may make recognition slightly early, though the chemical concept is robustly confirmed.
uncertainties: Clinical validation is incomplete
Compound discovery: PROTAC versus molecular glue and the thalidomide mechanism may require distinct credit
Priority between early PROTAC work and later small-molecule versions

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Multidimensional and relaxation-based solution NMR made it possible to determine structure and dynamics of large biomolecules in solution, including weakly populated states. Its importance to physical chemistry and structural biology is lasting, and the dynamics aspect resonates strongly with thermodynamic views of molecular motion.
assessment.attribution: Bax, Kay and Clore are the leading figures in methods (triple resonance, TROSY-based approaches, residual dipolar couplings, paramagnetic relaxation enhancement). Wagner and Palmer are also decisive in different parts, so a three-person selection leaves a visible gap, and NMR was recognised in 1991 and 2002.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, extensively confirmed and widely used for decades. Recognition is late rather than early, which is not a negative on merit.
uncertainties: Prior NMR Nobel Prizes may count against another NMR award
Choosing three among Bax, Kay, Clore, Wagner and Palmer is contestable

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape and funnel theory gave protein folding a statistical-mechanical basis and resolved Levinthal's paradox, linking thermodynamics, frustration and kinetics. It is a general physical-chemical principle with consequences for design, structure prediction and aggregation, and fits my soft-matter perspective.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic (with Bryngelson) are the principal architects of funnel theory; Dill contributed the hydrophobic-collapse and lattice-model framework. Fersht's experimental mapping is complementary and arguably equally deserving, making a pure theory prize versus a theory-plus-experiment configuration unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Concepts are deeply established and later vindicated by experiments and by structure prediction advances (2024 prize is adjacent), so there is a risk the field is considered already recognised.
uncertainties: The 2024 prize to Baker, Hassabis and Jumper on protein design and prediction may reduce appetite
Theory versus experiment attribution
I have not verified exact priority claims

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Self-assembled monolayers established molecular-level control of interfaces by spontaneous organisation, and soft lithography extended it into a patterning toolbox. This is a core interface and self-assembly concept with wide effect on surface science, biosensing and microfabrication.
assessment.attribution: Nuzzo and Allara reported the alkanethiolate-on-gold SAM system (1983), Whitesides developed it broadly and soft lithography; Sagiv's earlier silane monolayers are an important priority issue, and Xia contributed to soft lithography.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with decades of independent confirmation; recognition would be belated, and the Sagiv priority question could complicate the configuration.
uncertainties: Priority between Sagiv and Nuzzo/Allara
Whether soft lithography and SAMs should be treated as one prize
Possible view that the area is incremental relative to other candidates

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Machine-learned interatomic potentials combine near quantum accuracy with force-field cost, enabling simulations of liquids, interfaces and phase transitions that were out of reach. This is a transformative method for physical chemistry and materials, though its full impact is still unfolding.
assessment.attribution: Behler and Parrinello introduced neural-network potentials (2007); Csányi and Bartók developed Gaussian approximation potentials; von Lilienfeld, E and others contributed additional strands. Parrinello also appears in Car-Parrinello and metadynamics candidates, so any recognition for him could be configured elsewhere.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly maturing and increasingly validated, but transferability and reliability issues remain, so it may be slightly early.
uncertainties: Maturity: generalisation limits and rapid evolution of the field
Interaction with other Parrinello-linked candidates
Choosing among Behler, Csányi, Bartók, E and von Lilienfeld

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion lets cells incorporate noncanonical amino acids site-specifically, giving chemists the ability to install new chemistry in proteins in vivo. The concept is original and widely applied in biophysics, probes and therapeutics, though not my own specialty.
assessment.attribution: Schultz established the orthogonal tRNA/synthetase approach in cells and Chin extended it to multiple codons and eukaryotes and to genome recoding; Wang, Mehl and Yokoyama have key contributions, so credit is not unique.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and widely used for over two decades, so timely, with ongoing developments in genome recoding.
uncertainties: Allocation among Schultz, Chin, Wang, Mehl and Yokoyama
Overlap with prior recognition of directed evolution and phage display
My expertise in this area is limited
